supersedes.note: the Stage 1 ledger is kept unchanged as the historical record; this successor ledger corrects its evidence vocabulary

correctionReason: The Stage 1 ledger labelled exploratory observations 'VERIFIED', including one statement of NO effect (#361 H1). A null hypothesis that was not rejected is not a verified absence of effect.
It grouped every non-rejected registered claim as 'failedClaims', which reads as 'shown false'. They are claims the registered test did not support, at that test's power.
It reported P1's power from a binomial that treated the monthly alarm rate as a per-episode hit probability; Stage 2 measured that this test's real size is about 0.28, not 0.05.

evidenceTiers.EXPLORATORY_OBSERVATION: measured on outcome-exposed history; a description or estimate, not a tested prediction
evidenceTiers.STATISTICALLY_UNSUPPORTED: a registered test did not reject its null at that test's power; NOT evidence that the effect is absent
evidenceTiers.CONFIRMED_FUTURE_PREDICTIVE_POWER: confirmed on data not available when the hypothesis was fixed (prospective receipts)
evidenceTiers.VALIDATED_INVESTMENT_PERFORMANCE: a confirmed forecast transmitted into an executable allocation that beat its benchmark after costs prospectively
evidenceTiers.STRUCTURAL_OR_SOURCE_FACT: a fact about data availability, definitions or sample structure; makes no claim about returns

entries.statement: In every US/KR exposure overlay measured so far, the return gap to passive is almost entirely average exposure (LEVEL), not TIMING.
entries.correctedNote: repeated across studies on exposed history; an accounting decomposition of past paths, not a forecast

entries.statement: The estimated equity response to FOMC shocks is concentrated in the shock month (MP about -1.14%/SD, partly an identity of the JK classification).
A difference between MP and CBI shocks in subsequent 12-month excess return was not detected (+0.04pp, p 0.988, Holm 1.0).
entries.correctedNote: the null was not rejected; no equivalence test was registered, so 'no effect' is not established

entries.statement: After information-type shocks real yields were higher (+0.21/+0.22pp at 6/12 months) and breakevens lower; no EBP response was detected.
entries.correctedNote: no multiplicity correction; descriptive channel estimates

entries.statement: Loss frequency in credit-stress cells was 0-15% in 1970-89 and 12-69% in 1990-2024.
Trend/volatility probabilities had +4.6% Brier skill over the base rate for 6-month loss (1990-2024).
entries.correctedNote: out-of-sample in time but on exposed history and not a registered primary test

entries.statement: Adding valuation, earnings and credit to trend/volatility made out-of-sample 12-month loss forecasts worse (Brier +0.0043, p 0.033).
entries.correctedNote: a single exposed-history comparison; not a proof that these variables can never add information

entries.statement: Fast volatility is the clearest descriptive link to near-term KR downside; curve re-steepening after inversion matters more than inversion.

FAST was normal at some month-end in the 126 sessions before each of the 7 US -15% first passages since 1993; only 5 of them can be evaluated in real time because the first two are needed for training.
Real-time BAA and GS10 vintages exist from 1996-12-03; the month-end as-of credit series runs 1996-12..2026-10 with a ~1-2 month observation lag.
Trailing PE below its 5-year mean raising 12-month SPY excess return was not supported (+5.23pp, Holm p 0.184; fragile to 2021; no crisis in the sample).
Pure timing from the VM1T rule was not detected (+0.03pp/yr net); its gap to SPY is LEVEL.
The 8-cell valuation x SPF earnings x credit model did not beat valuation alone (dBrier -0.00087, p 0.664, Holm 1.0).
entries.correctedNote: the triple cell had 4 training months; the test had little power for it

entries.statement: Pure timing from #361's loss forecasts was not detected (-0.00pp/yr, p 0.986).
KR exposure ladders C1-C3 did not beat C0/passive; their return cost exceeded the drawdown value on that history.
US dynamic multi-asset rules did not beat the static mix; their defence came from 2008 alone and they lagged after 2016.

WITHDRAWN: Stage 1's episode-level power (3/7 hits needed at a 10% budget, power 0.77) assumed the monthly alarm rate was the per-episode hit probability. With each episode's 4-5 FAST-normal opportunities and the flag's persistence, 3 of 5 hits occur with probability about 0.28 under the null.

openCompetingExplanations: Credit stress is coincident with, not ahead of, equity breaks (both respond to the same news); P1 tests the lead directly.
Any credit lead is regime-specific (post-1990 credit-driven crises) and will not persist (Goyal-Welch instability).
Drawdown onsets are dominated by fast exogenous shocks (2020, 2025) that no monthly macro signal can lead.
Monthly-average credit with a ~1-2 month observation lag is too slow for 126-session onsets; daily PIT credit is unavailable before 2014.
